mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: Equity put/call ratio spikes above 1.2 during the signal period, indicating a contrarian sentiment washout that will lead to a short squeeze and positive returns.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected jump in the unemployment rate, signaling a rapidly weakening labor market, will trigger a risk-off sentiment shift and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: High-yield credit spreads tighten by more than 50 basis points during the signal period, indicating a 'bad news is good news' dynamic where weak economic data is expected to prompt monetary easing.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising consumer confidence (as measured by the Conference Board index) and falling mortgage rates will boost housing starts and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The spread between new and existing home sales inverts, indicating speculative excess that will lead to a housing market correction and negative spillover effects on consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A flattening of the yield curve, as measured by the spread between 10-year and 2-year Treasury yields, signals impending monetary tightening that will compress equity valuations and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: 10y-2y spread narrows by > 20 basis points in one month
failure_condition: The Fed unexpectedly cuts rates by 50 basis points or more during the signal period, reversing the tightening impulse and sparking a relief rally.

mechanism_narrative: An accelerating wage-price spiral, as measured by the year-over-year change in average hourly earnings and the core PCE deflator, will lead to a hawkish Fed response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed announces a strategic shift to average inflation targeting during the signal period, allowing for a more accommodative policy stance that will cushion equity valuations.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in retail sales, indicating a sudden collapse in consumer demand, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as companies scramble to cut earnings guidance.
failure_condition: The White House announces a new round of fiscal stimulus checks during the signal period, providing a quick boost to consumer spending power and averting the earnings downgrade cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in the ISM manufacturing index, indicating strong supply chain momentum, will boost S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies benefit from improved operating leverage and upward earnings revisions.
candidate_trigger: ISM manufacturing new orders index rises > 60 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The Baltic Dry Index plunges by > 30% during the signal period, indicating a global trade slowdown that will undermine the domestic manufacturing recovery.
